## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, recording 287 matching passages across 31 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. The most substantial reuse occurs in commentary literature—specifically both volumes of the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā* and the *Apadāna-aṭṭhakathā*—as well as numerous related biographical poems within the *Therāpadāna*, such as the *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3), *Ekachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 414), and *Upasivattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 407) [DharmaNexus]. Shared formulaic passages, especially around segments 43–45, are also found across many other *Therāpadāna* texts, including those of Sabbadāyaka (Tha-Ap 401), Jatukaṇṇi (Tha-Ap 411), and Bhaddāli (Tha-Ap 413) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus generates cross-language alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan texts, identifying shared phraseology in the Sanskrit *Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra* and *Suvarṇaprabhāsasūtra*, as well as Tibetan translations of the *Amitābhavyūhasūtra*, the *Jātakamālā*, and the *Mahāmeghasūtra* [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog and DharmaNexus data.*
